students.name: Chenran Weng
students.quote: ASWANI Professor , Industrial Engineering and Operations Research University of California, at Berkeley About Me I am a professor in industrial engineering and operations research (IEOR) at the University of California, at Berkeley . I received a BS in electrical engineering from the University of Michigan, in Ann Arbor , and a PhD in electrical engineering and computer sciences with a designated emphasis in computational and genomic biology from the University of California, at Berkeley. I have received an NSF CAREER award through the Operations Engineering program for my work on personalized healthcare, a Hellman Fellowship for my research on food insecurity, and the Leon O. Chua award from Berkeley for outstanding achievement in an area of nonlinear science. My research interests include data-driven decision making, with particular emphasis on improving health systems and physical infrastructure. students.name: Kanghyun Ryu
students.quote: Mehr Negar is an assistant professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Berkeley. The focus of her research is to develop control algorithms that allow autonomous systems to safely and intelligently interact with each other and with humans. Postdocs Lasse Peters Lasse is a postdoctoral scholar in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Berkeley. He develops algorithms that let robots handle complex physical and social interaction, from contact-rich manipulation and agile flight to anticipating the behavior of surrounding humans and robots. His work combines reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and dynamic game theory to learn policies and interaction models from limited data and to keep robots safe under model uncertainty, with validation on manipulators, mobile robots, and quadrotors. Prior to Berkeley, he completed his PhD at the Department of Cognitive Robotics at Delft University of Technology, where he wrote his dissertation on “Game-Theoretic Motion Planning for Multi-Agent Interaction”. Hongrui Zhao Hongrui is a postdoctoral scholar in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Berkeley. He is interested in developing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that generalize. Prior to Berkeley, he completed his PhD at the Department of Aerospace Engineering at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he wrote his dissertation on “Mapping the world together: collaborative neural implicit mapping under communication constraints”. students.quote: Abrahamson Post docs Graduate Students Research–Practice Partners Visiting Scholars Undergraduates Alumni Vision Projects All Projects (including previous ones) Embodied Professional Development Geometry Resources in Dance (GRiD) Kinemathics MOVES-Number Line OЯTHO Special Education Embodied Design (SpEED) Students Tracking Angular Rotation Recorder (STARR) TeleTangibles TriO Publications Design Glossary Workshops Courses Resources Home Website update request EDRL Research Group EDRL Physical Resources Qualifying Exam Lists EDRL Graduate Theses Grant Proposals 101 Conferences User Login Embodied Professional Development The PD focuses on geometry content, where the central activity, the Embodied Icosahedron, involves teacher groups in collaborative learning-by-building of a body-scale geometrical structure, an activity developed within the embodied design research framework. TeleTangibles The project’s vision is to inclusively bring hands-on, embodied learning into the current educational landscape through the launch of a new genre of STEM resources that the team calls TeleTangible a set of flexible. OЯTHO OЯTHO is a two-player, large-tabletop game at Copernicus Science Centre that has partners co-move a ball with orthogonal controls, cultivating “coordinate perception”. Students Tracking Angular Rotation Recorder (STARR) STARR engages learners in a culturally situated mathematical activity involving two participants in a constructed planetarium. Geometry Resources in Dance (GRiD) GRiD is a gridded floor mat designed to bridge the discourse of mathematics and dance. MOVES-Number Line Students solve basic addition and subtraction problems on a body-scale walking NL. Graduate Students Ellie Chew I am currently a first-year PhD student in the SESAME program. I wonder how people understand physics through play in museum installations and entertainment media outside of the classroom, and what continued play can look like in higher education. Emma Teresa (Ter) Booth My curiosities relate to the integration of STEAM learning into trauma-informed education practices. Drawing on enactivist theory, I am interested in designing and studying mathematics learning environments where learners can improve somatic awareness through exploring relationships, monitoring internal experiences, and representing discovered patterns within a logical framework. Erin Foley I study how multimodal engagements with data through improved access to the core aspects of working with data can facilitate data literacy and data visualization literacy. Jacqueline Anton

students.name: Kelly Easterday
students.quote: Maggi Kelly - Professor and Cooperative Extension Specialist Maggi has been at UC Berkeley since 1999 as a Professor and Cooperative Extension Specialist. Her working life is dedicated to all things geospatial. She loves maps! She works to bring cutting-edge mapping technology, training, and research support to the ANR and UC network of students, staff, faculty, and the public. Her group of students, staff, and postdocs (from UC Berkeley and UCANR) use a range of geospatial analysis approaches using data from numerous sources - spatial models, remote sensing, drones, lidar, historical archives, surveys, participatory mapping, and the field - to gain insights about how and why California landscapes are changing, and what that change means for those who live on, use, cherish, and manage our lands. The spatial data science field is evolving quickly, and Maggi actively works to build community around applied geospatial research and outreach locally at UC Berkeley and across the state. She is Faculty Director of the UCB Geospatial Innovation Facility ( GIF ) and Director of the ANR Statewide Program in Informatics and Geographic Information Systems ( IGIS ), both of which are dedicated to research, outreach and service in support of applied geospatial data and analysis. I do not have any students in my lab at the moment, and I am not accepting new graduate students at this time. But, if you would like to read about the IGIS crew, please do so here !
